KS-911.title: KS-907 launcher residues: a sentinel comment describing a test that does not exist, and a 2>/dev/null placed after the append it silences
KS-911.description:
## BLUF

**Two residues in** `Launch_Claude.command` **from the KS-907 by-hash gate (F1, F2 — both Minor). One is a comment describing a test that does not exist; the other is a** `2>/dev/null` **placed *after* the append it is meant to silence, so a failed open still prints. Both reproduced here before filing.**

⚠ **Ships by the BY-HASH mechanism, not as an in-place edit.** The hash that passed the gate (`9609c8453da8d7743a4b3ed2a94db6b09bef588c29f83e57b16255963a0929f1`) is the hash that runs. Any fix takes a new `.pre-` copy, the three hashes in the READY, and a narrow tier-2 gate on the diff — the same shape KS-907 used.

## F1 — a sentinel comment that describes a test that does not exist

`Launch_Claude.command:244`:

```
# ── KS-907 SEAT REGISTRY — BEGIN (do not edit the sentinels; the test extracts here) ──
```

The suite does **not** extract between the sentinels. It runs the real launcher via `SECUURA_LAUNCH_DRY_RUN=1` and parses the `DRY_RUN_*` markers — which is the better design, and it is what shipped. The sentinel wording is left over from a design that was replaced.

Measured: `Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh` contains **0** references to `KS-907 SEAT REGISTRY`, against a control of **2** occurrences of `SECUURA_LAUNCH_DRY_RUN=1` — so the suite really does not touch the sentinels, and the same grep can find what is there.

Consequence: nothing guards the sentinels, and the comment tells a future editor to preserve something for a reason that is not true. This is the same class as the KS-904 slip in the same session — a comment asserting a guard that is not in the code.

**Fix shape:** either delete the sentinels and the claim, or make them real by having the suite assert exactly one `BEGIN` and one `END`. Prefer the first: the dry-run markers already are the contract, and a second contract nothing checks is worse than none.

## F2 — `2>/dev/null` placed after the append it is meant to silence

`Launch_Claude.command:292` and `:295`:

```
printf '%s' "$SEAT_KEPT" > "$SEAT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
printf '%s|%s\n' "$$" "$SEAT_SELF_STARTED" >> "$SEAT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
```

Redirections apply left to right. The file is opened **before** `2>/dev/null` takes effect, so a failed open writes its error to the still-live stderr. The `|| true` swallows the status but not the noise, and a boot that cannot write its registry prints a bare shell error into the operator's pane.

Reproduced under `/bin/bash 3.2.57` — the shell the launcher runs under, not the zsh this repo's tooling defaults to:

|  | stderr |
| -- | -- |
| **A** `>> file 2>/dev/null` (the shipped shape) | `/bin/bash: line 2: /nonexistent-dir-xyz/f: No such file or directory` |
| **B** `2>/dev/null >> file` (redirect first) | *(none)* |
| **control** — a successful append, shape A | *(none)* |

The control matters: shape A is not simply always noisy, so the difference is the ordering and not the instrument.

*(An earlier A/B of mine did not discriminate because the Bash tool runs **zsh**, where both orderings reported the error.* `BASH_VERSION` *was empty — that is the tell.)*

**Fix shape:** move the redirection ahead of the target, at both sites.

## Regression

A launch whose registry directory is unwritable must produce no shell error on stderr — with a control launch that writes successfully, so the cell can fail.

Residues of the KS-907 tier-2 by-hash gate (F1, F2; Minor). Parent: KS-907.

nodes.body:
**BUILT and READY FOR QA — held for the gate. Ships BY HASH with KS-912 as one change; the launcher is at the project root, outside git, so there is no PR and no pre-push hook.**

| file | sha256 |
|---|---|
| `Launch_Claude.command` **(shipped)** | `932a2cc3aebe6cf838bf885ac92eec08e259f0572c0e08910088ac58e269f55c` |
| `Launch_Claude.command.pre-ks911` | `9609c8453da8d7743a4b3ed2a94db6b09bef588c29f83e57b16255963a0929f1` |
| `Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh` (guard, KS-912) | `b93b2c838e8766a8dc2b72e24d2f6fab21f9b912772e52328d43996414f18888` |

**The `.pre-` copy's hash equals KS-907's gated hash exactly**, so the baseline I changed is provably the file that passed that gate and nothing drifted in between. 23 changed lines. Mode unchanged (`-rwx------`).

⚠ **The change is live the moment the file changed** — the next boot of either seat reads it. On a NO GO the restore is one `cp` from `.pre-ks911`.

## F1 — the sentinel comment is gone, not made true

`:244` said *"do not edit the sentinels; the test extracts here"*. Measured now: **0** occurrences of `KS-907 SEAT REGISTRY` in the suite, against a **control of 2** occurrences of `SECUURA_LAUNCH_DRY_RUN=1` — so the suite really does parse the `DRY_RUN_*` markers, and the same grep can find what is there. `the test extracts here` now appears **0** times in the launcher.

Took the ticket's preferred option: deleted the claim rather than inventing a second contract. The replacement header records *why* it went and points at the real contract, so this does not simply become an unexplained deletion. The `END` marker is kept as a plain lowercase comment — it is navigation, not a sentinel, and it now reads as such.

## F2 — the redirect ordering, both sites

`2>/dev/null` now precedes the target at both write sites. Reproduced on the **shipped** file first:

| fixture | pre-fix stderr | reaches |
|---|---|---|
| unwritable **directory** (`TMPDIR` under `/dev/null`) | `line 295: … Not a directory` | the append only |
| existing but **read-only file** (`chmod 444`) | `line 292: … Permission denied` **and** `line 295: … Permission denied` | **both sites** |
| **control** — writable registry | *(silent)* | — |

The read-only-file fixture is the one the regression cell uses, because it is the only one that reaches **both** lines the ticket names. The writable control matters: the shipped shape is not simply always noisy, so what is being measured is the ordering.

In every fixture the launcher **still exited 0 and still emitted its `DRY_RUN` markers**, which is the control that makes an empty stderr mean something — an empty stderr from a launcher that died on line one looks identical to a clean one.

## Regression cell — CASE 6 in the KS-912 suite

Asserts no shell error on stderr with an unwritable registry, **gated on the run having reached its markers**, plus a writable control.

**Red-proof — the fixed suite against `Launch_Claude.command.pre-ks911`:**

```
fixed launcher    18 passed, 0 failed
pre-fix launcher  17 passed, 1 failed   <- CASE 6 alone
```

Only CASE 6 flips. Its own control stays green, and the other 16 cells stay green, so the cell discriminates rather than the run simply falling over.

**Side effects checked after every run:** `2_Project_Files/.git/config` byte-identical (`75c96972…`), `.launch_preflight_last.txt` restored byte-identical. Seat A's checkout untouched — the launcher runs no `pull`, `fetch` or `checkout` against it, only `git config` writes, which is what that assertion covers.

**BLUF — re-verified 2026-11-05 on the launcher every launch runs today (`4f519a6b…`): both KS-911 fixes are intact (all 19 added lines present, all 4 removed lines absent; 23 changed lines in all) and the guard suite passes 18/0 on it, run in place. Held for the tier-1 QA gate. This seat changed, swapped and merged nothing.**

**Why this comment exists.** The 2026-09-06 READY gates `932a2cc3…f55c`. That file is no longer what runs and is not on disk. It is reproduced exactly (below); the distance to the live file is four later edits, none of them KS-911 or KS-912.

| state | sha256 (start) | bytes | step from the row above |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.pre-ks911` | `9609c845…` | 36,087 | KS-907's gated file, the KS-911 baseline |
| shipped (ticket) | `932a2cc3…` | 37,076 | KS-911: 23 changed lines. **Not on disk; rebuilt, see below** |
| `.pre-0914-keepalive` | `9b301721…` | 37,093 | TURN-END RULE prompt wording, 1 line. No `.pre-` copy was taken for this edit |
| `.pre-0922-1814-nofetch` | `35413bab…` | 37,197 | keepalive: `ServerAliveInterval` on the two ssh option strings |
| `.pre-1027-model` | `65f63232…` | 37,262 | nofetch: boot git-sync wording `git fetch` becomes `git ls-remote` |
| **live** | `4f519a6b…` | 39,821 | model: the `SEAT_MODEL` block and `exec claude --model "$SEAT_MODEL"` |

Full hashes:
```
9609c8453da8d7743a4b3ed2a94db6b09bef588c29f83e57b16255963a0929f1  .pre-ks911
932a2cc3aebe6cf838bf885ac92eec08e259f0572c0e08910088ac58e269f55c  shipped (ticket), rebuilt
9b3017215b4d5093098166079b1417ab189796353b020df1865eaa3af203bf72  .pre-0914-keepalive
35413bab27864a0e9d407bcdb522dcabe36a221cae205c1cec5f53cb31bb874c  .pre-0922-1814-nofetch
65f63232240d15c6336cc0c300bd31fe72b5afcaab9ed56cbb1878b8e709b5b5  .pre-1027-model
4f519a6b631623221f64b0dfc61321c3dbf6378f463e9f60dcb8f42022cd42c2  live Launch_Claude.command
b93b2c838e8766a8dc2b72e24d2f6fab21f9b912772e52328d43996414f18888  Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh (unchanged since 2026-09-06)
```

**Rebuild of the shipped hash.** `.pre-0914-keepalive` with only its TURN-END RULE line put back to the `.pre-ks911` wording has sha256 `932a2cc3…f55c`, equal to the ticket's. The unmodified file does not match (control). The order of the three later edits is confirmed from their content, not only from file names and sizes.

**KS-911 lines in the live file.** `.pre-ks911` to shipped is 5 hunks and 23 changed lines, which is the ticket's count. Each added block is present in live as an exact contiguous block (live lines 244, 246-253, 300-307, 310, 380) and each of the 4 removed lines is absent from live. Controls: the added blocks are present in the shipped file, the removed lines in the baseline. The END marker moved from 379 to 380 because the nofetch edit adds one line above it.

**F1.** `the test extracts here`: live 0 hits, `.pre-ks911` 1 (positive control). The suite has 0 references to `KS-907 SEAT REGISTRY` and 2 to `SECUURA_LAUNCH_DRY_RUN=1`.

**F2**, executed under `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 (the launcher's shell) on the exact write-site lines, live `:307` and `:310` against pre-fix `:292` and `:295`:

| registry | pre-fix lines | live lines |
|---|---|---|
| read-only file (`chmod 444`) | 2 error lines | 0 |
| unwritable path (parent is a file) | 2 error lines | 0 |
| writable file (control) | silent | silent |

End to end: the suite's CASE 6 passes on live and is the only cell that fails on `.pre-ks911` (17 passed, 1 failed), with its writable CONTROL still passing.

**Suite** (`b93b2c83…`), `TMPDIR` isolated to the seat's work folder: live launcher, suite run in place at the project root, 18 passed / 0 failed, 8 launcher runs; the same files as hash-verified copies in a sandbox workspace, 18/0. `2_Project_Files/.git/config` byte-identical. Every launcher run overwrites `.launch_preflight_last.txt` (line 91, before the dry-run exit); the suite's own trap restored it byte-identical. `.claude/settings.local.json` is rewritten with identical bytes (mtime changes only).

**NOT run, and limits.**
- The suite's dry run stops before `exec claude`. The exec line is exercised only by real launches; this seat booted on `4f519a6b…` at 04:27:17Z.
- The three later edits are not part of this change and were not gated here. The only checks on them: they do not touch the 23 lines, and the suite passes with them.
- Other projects' launchers are per-project copies of the template. None was read or changed; the fix lives in this copy only.
- F5 stays a declared limit. Live reading: CASE 5 counted 3 sessions at the live path (the fabricated one, this seat, and a harness shell whose command text contains `claude ` and the project path).

Record: `5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatK-15th/` (`evidence/hash_reconcile.tsv`, `evidence/f_checks.tsv`, `evidence/suite_*.out`). Done and archive wait for the gate verdict.

KS-912.title: KS-907 suite residues: CASE 2 never asserts the pruning it is named for, a cell count printed as a launcher-run count, and a grep -qc diagnostic
KS-912.description:
## BLUF

**Three residues in** `Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh` **from the KS-907 by-hash gate (F3, F4, F6 — all Polish). The worst is F4: CASE 2, the cell the suite calls "the one that matters most", never asserts the thing it is named for. All three reproduced here before filing.**

Ships with the launcher follow-up by the same by-hash mechanism — the suite sits at the project root, outside git, like the launcher.

## F4 — CASE 2 asserts the consequence, not the act

CASE 2 exists to prove that a **dead** registry entry is *pruned*, because a guard that latched on a stale PID would pin every future launch of the project into read-only mode. It asserts `DRY_COUNT = 0` and that the step carries the pull text — both of which are the *downstream effect*. **It never checks that the dead pid left the file.**

So a launcher that read the entry, counted it as not-live, and left it in the registry forever would pass CASE 2 while the file grew without bound.

**Fix shape:** assert the dead pid is absent from `$SEAT_FILE` after the run, and — the control that makes it discriminate — that the *live* pid in CASE 1 is still **present**. Presence and absence in the same batch.

## F3 — the hygiene cell prints the cell count and calls them launcher runs

The label is built from `$((pass+fail))`:

> `2_Project_Files/.git/config is byte-identical after 12 launcher runs`

**12 is the number of cells that had run at that point. The true number of launcher invocations is 6** — measured: `run_launcher` is called exactly 6 times (control, live, dead, recycled, scan, scanoff).

The assertion itself is sound; only the number in the sentence is wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that overstates the evidence. The figure `12` was carried into KS-907's READY and its ticket comment; both are corrected to 6.

**Fix shape:** count the invocations in `run_launcher` and print that.

## F6 — `grep -qc` with `echo $?` as a diagnostic

`Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh:98`, inside the CONTROL's failure message:

```
pull-text=$(grep -qc "$PULLTEXT" "$WORK/control.step" 2>/dev/null; echo $?)
```

`-q` and `-c` contradict: `-q` wins, so nothing is counted and the `echo $?` prints an exit status labelled as if it were a count. It appears only in a `bad()` message, so it has never been rendered — which is exactly why it survived.

**Fix shape:** use the same `grep -q … && echo YES || echo NO` form the neighbouring field already uses.

## Declared limit, recorded not fixed (F5)

The process scan matches the project directory as a **substring** of the argv, so a sibling project directory named `Blockchain-<anything>` would be counted as a seat of this project. No such sibling exists (measured). The failure direction is safe — a false positive costs a read-only boot — and it is recorded on KS-907 as a limit rather than worked.

Residues of the KS-907 tier-2 by-hash gate (F3, F4, F6; Polish). Parent: KS-907.

nodes.body:
**BUILT and READY FOR QA — ships BY HASH with KS-911 as one change.** `Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh` **(shipped)** sha256 `b93b2c838e8766a8dc2b72e24d2f6fab21f9b912772e52328d43996414f18888`; `.pre-ks912` sha256 `a5d5d9ef8bd3e1039e3ee89b6334356644939f91b76c5002fef41e0dca554901` — **equal to KS-907's gated hash**, so the baseline is provably that gate's file. 75 changed lines. Suite **18 passed, 0 failed**.

## F4 — done FIRST, as directed. CASE 2 now asserts the thing it is named for.

Two assertions, presence and absence, in the same batch:

- **CASE 1 (presence):** after a run with a genuinely live seat, that pid is **still in** `$SEAT_FILE`.
- **CASE 2 (absence):** after a run with a dead entry, that pid is **gone from** `$SEAT_FILE`.

Without the presence half, a launcher that simply cleared the registry every run would satisfy "the dead pid is gone" for entirely the wrong reason.

**Red-proof — a parked tamper that counts a dead entry but never writes the pruned set back** (`Launch_Claude.command.KS912-TAMPER-noprune.parked`, sha256 `21a1ec04f7bc2e89f96475df42c4cb22c0292e0cb92539150e3f734656ec6ced`, **2 changed lines**, the prune write-back made a no-op and nothing else):

```
  ok   …and the LIVE entry is still IN the registry after the run (kept, not cleared)
  ok   CASE 2's precondition holds — PID 68301 is really dead
  ok   a DEAD entry is pruned → the launch is a single seat again, not latched read-only   <- THE OLD CELL, PASSING
  FAIL …and the DEAD pid is GONE from the registry                                          <- THE NEW ONE
       PID 68301 is STILL in …/secuura-launch-seats/… — counted as not-live but never
       removed, so the file grows without bound

  17 passed, 1 failed
```

**That is the finding, demonstrated:** on a launcher that never prunes, the cell CASE 2 already had **passes**, and only the new assertion catches it. The count and the pull text were the downstream effect all along.

## F3 — the label counts launcher runs now

`LAUNCH_RUNS` is incremented inside `run_launcher` itself, so it cannot drift from the call sites. The suite now prints *"byte-identical after **8** launcher runs"*.

Verified independently rather than trusting the new counter: 9 grep hits for `run_launcher` in the file, **one of which is a comment**, so **8** real invocations — control, live, dead, recycled, scan, scanoff, and the two CASE 6 runs this change adds. Matches. (The old figure would now read **18**, the cell count — the same overstatement, larger.)

## F6 — the diagnostic reports a fact instead of an exit status

`grep -qc … ; echo $?` → `grep -q … && echo YES || echo NO`. A/B on the same file:

```
OLD  grep -qc + echo $?   -> 0      an EXIT STATUS printed where a count was implied
NEW  present string       -> YES
NEW  absent string        -> NO     CONTROL: the new form discriminates
```

## Also in this change

**CASE 6**, the regression cell for KS-911 F2 — it lives in this suite, so it ships here. Details on KS-911.

## Not fixed, and why

**F5** (the process scan matching the project directory as an argv substring) stays recorded as a declared limit on KS-907, not worked. The failure direction is safe — a false positive costs a read-only boot, never another seat's branch — and no sibling directory that would trigger it exists.

**BLUF — re-verified 2026-11-05: the suite shipped for KS-912 is byte-for-byte the file on disk (`b93b2c83…`, unchanged since 2026-09-06), F3, F4 and F6 are fixed and each re-proved with a control, and the parked red-proof still makes the new F4 cell fail alone. 18 passed / 0 failed on the launcher every launch runs today. Held for the tier-1 QA gate; this seat changed, swapped and merged nothing. The launcher side of this change, and the hash chain from the gated `932a2cc3…` to the live `4f519a6b…`, are on KS-911.**

| file | sha256 | bytes |
|---|---|---|
| `Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh` (shipped, on disk) | `b93b2c838e8766a8dc2b72e24d2f6fab21f9b912772e52328d43996414f18888` | 18,059 |
| `Launch_Claude.seats.test.sh.pre-ks912` | `a5d5d9ef8bd3e1039e3ee89b6334356644939f91b76c5002fef41e0dca554901` | 13,930 |
| red-proof tamper, parked | `21a1ec04f7bc2e89f96475df42c4cb22c0292e0cb92539150e3f734656ec6ced` | 37,092 |

Both suite hashes equal the ones in the 2026-09-06 comment. The diff `.pre-ks912` to shipped is 7 hunks and 75 changed lines, which is the ticket's count. The tamper differs from the rebuilt shipped launcher in 2 lines: `Launch_Claude.command:307` writes nothing back (`: "$SEAT_KEPT"` replaces the `printf`).

**F4, CASE 2 now asserts the act.** Presence assertion at suite line 149 (the live pid is still in `$SEAT_FILE`), absence assertion at line 182 (the dead pid is gone). `.pre-ks912` has 0 assertions of either kind.

| suite | launcher | result |
|---|---|---|
| new | live | 18 passed / 0 failed |
| new | `.pre-ks911` | 17 / 1, only CASE 6 (the KS-911 F2 cell) |
| new | tamper (counts a dead entry, never prunes it) | 17 / 1, only "…and the DEAD pid is GONE from the registry"; "a DEAD entry is pruned → single seat" still passes |
| old (`.pre-ks912`) | tamper | **14 / 0, the old suite cannot see it** |
| old (`.pre-ks912`) | live | 14 / 0 |

**F3, the label counts launcher runs.** Independent count of `run_launcher` call sites: old suite 6, new suite 8 (lines 98, 133, 169, 199, 224, 238, 262, 277). Printed: old suite "byte-identical after **12** launcher runs", new suite "after **8** launcher runs". `LAUNCH_RUNS` is initialised at line 53 and incremented inside `run_launcher` at line 65.

**F6.** `grep -qc` occurrences: suite 0, `.pre-ks912` 1 (positive control). The defect itself, under `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 on a file with 3 matches: `grep -qc a f; echo $?` prints `0` (an exit status, no count) while `grep -c a f` prints `3`. The replacement form `grep -q … && echo YES || echo NO` appears 4 times in the suite.

**Run conditions.** `TMPDIR` pointed at the seat's work folder (the suite does `rm -f` on its registry path, so it must never share the real one); `bash` resolved to `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 for both the suite and the launcher. Run in place at the project root and again as hash-verified copies in a sandbox workspace, both 18/0. `2_Project_Files/.git/config` byte-identical; `.launch_preflight_last.txt` restored byte-identical by the suite's own trap.

**Candidate found while running it (not worked, no ticket filed):** the suite's cleanup kills the CASE 5 fixture's `sh -c 'sleep 300; :'` wrapper but not its `sleep 300` child. Every completed run left one orphan (9 of 9 runs; each expires after 300 s; stopped here by recorded pid).

**NOT run.** The suite does not exercise `exec claude`. Other projects' copies of the suite and launcher were not read or changed. F5 is a declared limit and is not worked.

Record: `5_Project_History/2026-11-05_seatK-15th/` (`evidence/f_checks.tsv`, `evidence/suite_*.out` and `.json`, `evidence/hash_reconcile.tsv`). Done and archive wait for the gate verdict.
